title: Belrose Promotional Financing Plans — Household Plan Cap and One Plan per Sales Receipt
content:
# Belrose Promotional Financing Plans — Household Plan Cap and One Plan per Sales Receipt

**Finance desk servicing rule.** The number of Belrose Promotional Financing Plans one customer may hold open at the same time is capped for the household as a whole at **4**, and a plan counts as open while it stands at applied, approved, active, past due or in a hardship arrangement. A plan that has closed settled, been written off or been cancelled never counts against the cap.

## The rule in clauses

1. A further promotional financing plan is opened for a customer only when no plan already recorded against the same sales receipt number stands at applied, approved, active, past due or in a hardship arrangement.
2. Where the cap of 4 open plans is already reached, the desk does not open a further plan and the customer is offered the reallocation of an existing plan instead.
3. Whether a plan counts as open is read from the status the plan record carries, never from what the customer says about it.

## Points of judgement

| Question the desk settles | Where the answer is read | What counts |
|---|---|---|
| Is there already a plan on this receipt? | The plan records carrying this customer's sales receipt number | A plan on that receipt number standing at applied, approved, active, past due or in a hardship arrangement blocks a further plan on the same receipt; a plan on that receipt that is settled, written off or cancelled does not |
| How many plans does the household hold open? | The status of every plan record of the customer | Each plan at applied, approved, active, past due or in a hardship arrangement counts one; settled, written off and cancelled plans count nothing |
| Is the cap reached? | The count above against the cap of 4 | At 4 open plans the cap is reached and no further plan is opened |

The receipt condition and the cap are separate conditions: a customer with two open plans on other receipts and one open plan on this receipt is blocked on this receipt by the first clause even though the household count of three stands under the cap of 4.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A customer holds three plans open on three different receipts and one plan that closed settled last year. The household count is three, under the cap of 4, and a further plan on a fresh receipt may be opened.
- A customer holds four plans open. The cap of 4 is reached; the desk does not open a further plan and offers the reallocation of an existing plan instead.
- A customer's earlier application on the same sales receipt still stands at applied. A further plan on that receipt is not opened, whatever the household count.
